description: IPv6 tunnel broker provider definitions (RFC 3053-style services) with protocol, routing and reachability metadata

status.description: Service lifecycle status: active = open registrations; restricted = signup gated (own ASN required, verified operators, manual approval); no_new_registrations = existing tunnels work but new ones cannot be created; discontinued = service shut down

type.description: Pricing classification of the tunnel service itself

protocols.description: Tunnel protocols offered: 6in4 = IPv6-in-IPv4 proto-41 (incl. SIT); 4in6 = IPv4-in-IPv6; ipip = IP-in-IP proto-4; ayiya = Anything In Anything (SixXS); tsp = Tunnel Setup Protocol; tic = Tunnel Information and Control (SixXS); heartbeat = draft-massar-v6ops-heartbeat

hosts.description: Additional provider domains beyond the record key (portal/manager hostnames, alternate service domains) for attribution

prefixes.description: Routed IPv6 prefix lengths handed to users per tunnel/subnet (e.g. 64, 56, 48); absent when the provider assigns no address space (BYOIP-only)

bgp.description: Whether BGP peering over the tunnel is offered

rdns.description: Whether reverse DNS (PTR) delegation for routed prefixes is offered

byoip.description: Whether users may announce their own PI/PA space or their own ASN over the tunnel

endpoint_update.description: How a dynamic client IPv4 endpoint is kept in sync: none = static endpoint required; dyndns2 = Dyn-compatible nic/update endpoint; http = provider-specific HTTP update URL; automatic = protocol handles roaming (e.g. WireGuard)

nat.description: Whether the service works behind NAT/CGNAT without a public IPv4 address

pops.description: Number of tunnel points of presence

locations.description: PoP locations as 'City, CC' strings (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country)

bandwidth_mbps.description: Documented per-tunnel bandwidth cap in Mbit/s

asn.description: Provider's own autonomous system number; absent when tunnels run under a sponsor AS

allocation.description: Provider's own IPv6 allocation(s) the tunnel space is drawn from, as CIDR strings

api.description: Whether programmatic provisioning/management (REST API or equivalent) exists

services.description: Additional network services beyond plain tunnels

until.description: Year the service ended (for discontinued providers)

public.description: Whether anyone can request a tunnel publicly. false = gated to verified operators, customers of other products, or invite-only.

oneOf.description: Verification method required during account creation
Verification methods required during account creation

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the provider's legal seat (from imprint/terms/operator info); absent = unknown
